summary.text: Late preterm female infant born at 35 + 1/7 weeks with prenatally diagnosed duodenal atresia, operated on the second day of life without complications.

Cerebral ultrasound showed bilateral parenchymal abnormalities (hyperechogenic periventricular matter and subependymal cysts); dried spots on DOL3 were negative, urine CMV DNA was positive on DOL51 and blood on DOL53; hearing tests were normal and other intrauterine infections were excluded.
Diagnosed with postnatally acquired CMV infection in a healthy baby who needed no treatment; followed to 12 months with normal neurodevelopment and no other sequelae.

Feeding intolerance with vomiting and abdominal distension from DOL15 (possible NEC), severe thrombocytopenia from DOL20 refractory to platelet transfusions, and persistent leukopenia.

article_limitations: Narrative review with a five-case series (Section 3, Table 1); Sections 1-2 and 4-11, Tables 2-3 and all figures are literature review or background and are not patient facts.
Table 1 columns 1-5 are mapped to Cases 1-5 by position; table viral loads and sex/milk rows carry no collection dates, so none were assigned.

Table 1 "N/A" for CMV DNA in maternal milk (Cases 1, 2, 4, 5) is legend-defined "not available" and was not recorded as a test; it neither establishes that the test was performed nor that milk was uninfected.
